name: Zionism
summary: Zionism is the nationalist movement holding that Jews are a people entitled to self-determination in a state of their own in the Land of Israel. It organized Jewish immigration and settlement, revived Hebrew and Jewish national culture, and founded the State of Israel in 1948; since then it has centered on sustaining Israel as a Jewish and democratic state, encouraging immigration, and securing it militarily. Its strands range from socialist to free-market and from secular to religious, so it has little common economic program.
scope: The shared core of mainstream Zionism as set out in Herzl's The Jewish State (1896), the Declaration of the Establishment of the State of Israel (1948) and the World Zionist Organization's Jerusalem Program, with Jabotinsky's Iron Wall for the security doctrine common to the mainstream, and contemporary attitudes drawn from Pew's survey of Israeli Jews. Economic and social questions where Labor, General, Revisionist and Religious Zionism differ are answered as split. Separate profiles exist for strands such as Labor Zionism; Christian Zionism, post-Zionism and anti-Zionist positions are excluded.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a Zionist plank as such; inferred from Herzl's concern for workers' welfare and the Labor movement's collective institutions, though liberal strands are less committed.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Labor Zionism built socialist and cooperative institutions while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement as a whole is split on wage policy.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Herzl promised to respect private property, but labor Zionism built socialist and cooperative institutions while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement as a whole is split.

public-ownership.rationale: Labor Zionism built socialist and cooperative institutions while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement as a whole is split on public ownership of industry.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Labor Zionism built socialist and cooperative institutions while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement as a whole is split on taxation.

unions-good.rationale: Labor Zionism was built around its labor federation, while Revisionists opposed its dominance, so adherents divide on unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Herzl called private property the basis of independence, yet the movement also made acquiring land as public national property a core task, so it is not treated as near-absolute.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Labor Zionism built socialist and cooperative institutions while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement as a whole is split; corporate regulation is not a Zionist question.

cut-welfare.rationale: Herzl wanted relief through work rather than charity, but the Labor strand built extensive social provision; the movement takes no common line.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective settlements were a Labor Zionist hallmark, but other strands did not share the aim, so the family is split.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the movement's priority on security against hostile neighbors; Zionist texts do not address surveillance directly.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Zionism has no position on drug policy; adherents vary with their wider politics.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The Jerusalem Program commits the movement to struggle against antisemitism, and most Israeli Jews see antisemitism as common and growing; support for legal limits on hate speech is inferred from that.

strong-leader.rationale: Herzl favored an aristocratic republic, but the founding Declaration commits the state to elected authorities and mainstream Zionism defines Israel as democratic.

state-harmful.rationale: Establishing a sovereign Jewish state is the movement's central goal; Herzl called it a world need.

limit-guns.rationale: Civilian gun ownership is not a Zionist question; strands differ.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Jerusalem Program calls for encouraging army and security service, and Jabotinsky argued that settlement could only proceed behind a strong defensive force.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: No Zionist position; secular and religious adherents would divide.

decide-locally.rationale: Zionism is a centrally organized national project; Herzl placed leadership in a single Society of Jews and Jewish Company. Inferred.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal policy is outside Zionist doctrine.

traditional-family.rationale: Religious Zionists strongly uphold traditional family structures while secular adherents are more liberal, so the family is divided.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Secular and religious Zionists split sharply on marriage law; Israel has no civil marriage and the issue divides the camp.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not a Zionist question; secular and religious adherents divide.

more-religion-public.rationale: Herzl wanted clergy kept within their temples and secular Jews favor separation, while religious Zionists want the state to promote Jewish religion; the split is documented.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Zionism frames Jews as a people recovering from persecution, but takes no general position on remedying racial injustice.

gender-social-construct.rationale: No Zionist position; adherents vary with their religiosity.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Reviving Jewish national culture and the Hebrew language, and Jewish and Zionist education, are listed foundations of the movement.

gradual-change.rationale: Weizmann's mainstream favored incremental state-building while Revisionists demanded an immediate state, and the project itself was a radical break with diaspora life.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Encouraging Jewish immigration (aliyah) from all countries is a core plank, so adherents oppose reducing it; the commitment concerns Jewish immigration specifically.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The founding Declaration pledged cooperation with the UN, but Zionism centers national sovereignty; the answer is inferred and not stated.

free-trade.rationale: Trade policy is outside Zionist doctrine and divides its economic strands.

nation-first.rationale: The movement exists to represent the national interests of the Jewish people and to secure them by its own strength, rather than relying on others' goodwill.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Herzl conceived the state as neutral; Zionism takes no general position on intervening abroad.

open-borders.rationale: A Jewish state requires a Jewish majority and control over who enters, which is incompatible with open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental limits on growth are not a Zionist question; the movement prized developing the land.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed by Zionist doctrine; adherents vary.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Herzl framed the return as a feat of modern organization and technology; inferred from that developmental optimism.

revolution-justified.rationale: Mainstream Zionism honors the armed struggle of the Haganah and other underground groups that helped end British rule and found the state.

experts-over-public.rationale: Herzl favored rule by a capable elite and distrusted referendums; later mainstream Zionism is democratic, so this is weak.

central-planning.rationale: Labor Zionism built socialist and cooperative institutions while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement as a whole is split on planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Labor Zionism built socialist and cooperative institutions while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement as a whole is split.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Labor Zionism built socialist and cooperative institutions while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement as a whole is split on taxation.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed by Zionist doctrine; strands differ.

state-directs-investment.rationale: National institutions such as Herzl's Jewish Company and later the movement's funds were designed to direct capital into settlement and development.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Strands differ between collective settlement and private enterprise.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Apart from collective settlements, mainstream Zionism assumed a money economy with respected private property.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred: a state-building movement that wants national financial institutions would not abolish central banking.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The Labor movement's federation played a quasi-corporatist role, but other strands opposed it.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Declaration commits the state to elected authorities and the Jerusalem Program to a Jewish and democratic state; Zionism has always been multi-party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Herzl considered a democratic monarchy or an aristocratic republic acceptable; the movement has no monarchist program.

democracy-best.rationale: Israel is defined as Jewish and democratic, and most Israeli Jews say it can be both, though religious adherents put religious law above democracy in a conflict.

direct-votes.rationale: Herzl judged referendums an unsatisfactory procedure; mainstream Zionism is parliamentary.

workers-councils.rationale: The movement founded a parliamentary state, not a council system.

right-to-secede.rationale: Zionism is itself a claim to national self-determination, but adherents reject partition of the land where it threatens the Jewish state; no clear general position.

natural-rulers.rationale: Herzl inclined to an aristocratic republic, but later mainstream Zionism is democratic; not a settled position.

political-violence-never.rationale: Jabotinsky argued settlement needed protection by force, and mainstream Zionism honors the armed struggle that founded the state.

war-builds-character.rationale: Zionist thought treats force as necessary for defense rather than as ennobling in itself.

separate-church-state.rationale: Secular Zionists favor separating religion from government, while religious Zionists want the state to promote Jewish values; the split is documented.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Founding Zionism was secular and most Israeli Jews oppose making religious law state law, though religious Zionists favor it.

private-courts-defense.rationale: National defense by a state army is central; the program calls for service in the national army and security forces.

military-superiority.rationale: The "iron wall" doctrine holds that Jewish security depends on strength adversaries cannot overcome.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Zionism defines Jews as one people entitled to a state with a Jewish majority, while promising equal citizenship to minorities.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Zionism treats the national question as primary; even Labor Zionism framed economic struggle in national terms.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Labor Zionism built socialist and cooperative institutions while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement as a whole is split.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Zionists regard Jews as indigenous to the Land of Israel and assert a historical right to it, while opposing competing Palestinian claims; the statement does not map onto a single answer.

civilizational-union.rationale: Zionism seeks a separate Jewish nation-state, not union with other states sharing a religion or civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Not addressed; strands range from collectivist to liberal.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The program stresses mutual Jewish responsibility, pioneering, and military or national service as duties to the nation.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed by mainstream Zionism; the movement valued working and developing the land.

limit-population.rationale: The movement seeks to grow the Jewish population of Israel through immigration; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Herzl envisaged a modern industrial state; the movement is developmental.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred from Herzl's reliance on modern technology and organization.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed by Zionist doctrine; adherents vary.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed by Zionist doctrine; adherents vary.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; security priorities might cut against it.

restore-past-order.rationale: Zionism sought national restoration in the ancestral homeland but as a modern, mostly secular project; religious Zionists stress redemption more.

direct-action.rationale: Herzl sought a charter through diplomacy and the movement governed itself through elected Zionist Congresses and later the Knesset, though practical Zionism also built facts through settlement; inferred from that mix.

means-match-ends.rationale: Jabotinsky's Iron Wall argues that force must secure the Jewish state first and that peace and equal rights come after, so the means need not mirror the end.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Never addressed directly, but the movement prides itself on reclaiming and farming the land and building modern towns, the opposite of a return to foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Kibbutzim rotated jobs, but the movement as a whole set out to build a full modern economy with every occupation; inferred from its nation-building aims.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Labor Zionism's kibbutzim shared by need while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement is split.

production-for-use.rationale: Socialist and free-market strands disagree on the purpose of production, and the movement has no shared economic program.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Labor Zionists drew on socialist ideas of exploitation while Herzl and the Revisionists defended private property and enterprise, so the movement is split.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Even socialist Zionism built its institutions through elections, and the state was founded on elected authorities; inferred from that democratic practice.

collective-farming.rationale: Collective kibbutzim and cooperative moshavim were Labor Zionism's model, but private farming and enterprise were also part of settlement, so the movement is split.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Zionism explains conflict through national and security terms rather than capitalism, and its liberal strands favored commerce; inferred from its nationalist framework.

taxation-theft.rationale: Herzl's plan relied on a public body raising funds and the movement built extensive public institutions, so it treats taxes as a legitimate part of statehood; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Secular strands are broadly liberal while Religious Zionists want Jewish law to shape public life, so adherents are split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Zionism rests on the collective right of the Jewish people to self-determination, stated in the Declaration as the natural right of the Jewish people.

conscription.rationale: The Jerusalem Program lists military and national service among Zionist duties, and Jabotinsky's security doctrine depends on a citizen army.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The movement grounded the state in elected institutions and seeks to bring Jews in rather than treating leaving as the check on government; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Herzl used a chartered Jewish Company for practical tasks but placed political authority in a public body and the state in an elected government.

media-academia-power.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from the movement's commitment to elected, democratic government as where power lies.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The Declaration promises equality irrespective of race, and the mainstream defines the Jewish people by history and peoplehood rather than biology; an inference about a question it did not address.

organic-representation.rationale: Zionist institutions and Israel are organized through parties and party lists, though Herzl toyed with an aristocratic republic; inferred from that practice.

total-state.rationale: The founding Declaration guarantees freedom of religion, conscience, language, education and culture, leaving those areas outside state direction.

national-rebirth.rationale: Zionism presents itself as the renewal of a people weakened by exile, through return, Hebrew and statehood, though not as a radical purge of decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Revisionist and Religious Zionists sought the whole Land of Israel while Labor Zionists accepted partition, so the mainstream is split beyond the core homeland.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The state is built on law, a constitution-to-be and elected authorities, not personal bonds; inferred from the Declaration.

bound-labor.rationale: The Declaration promises complete social and political equality, and Herzl proposed a seven-hour working day for free workers, which excludes serfdom.

knowledge-power.rationale: Herzl and the founders trusted modern science and education as neutral tools of national progress; inferred from that outlook.

universal-morality.rationale: The Declaration bases the state on liberty, justice and peace as envisaged by the prophets of Israel and on the UN Charter, implying universal moral principles; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Zionism is a coalition of socialist, liberal, religious and revisionist strands that compete in elections, so it balances interests rather than deriving one good; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: This is the movement's founding aim, stated by Herzl and enacted in the 1948 Declaration.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Encouraging aliyah and the ingathering of exiles is a listed foundation of Zionism, and the Declaration opens the state to Jewish immigration.

revive-national-language.rationale: The revival of Hebrew was a central Zionist project and stays in the Jerusalem Program's commitment to Hebrew education.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Labor Zionism built worker-run cooperative institutions such as the Histadrut and kibbutzim, while General and Revisionist Zionists favored private enterprise, so the movement is split. Inferred from the strands described in the Zionism article.

school-vouchers.rationale: Zionist programs stress Hebrew and Zionist education but do not specify how schools are funded, and Labor and free-market strands differ. Inferred from the Jerusalem Program's education aims.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Zionism has no common fiscal doctrine; Labor and General Zionists differed on state economic management and Revisionists favored private enterprise. Inferred from the economic divisions noted in the Zionism article.

economic-freedom.rationale: Herzl treated private property as a basis of independence while Labor Zionism built collective institutions and public land holding, so the movement has no common line on how economic and political freedom relate; inferred from its split economic strands.

missingStatements.text: The Jewish people have a right to a state of their own in the Land of Israel.
missingStatements.rationale: This is the movement's founding aim, stated by Herzl and enacted in the 1948 Declaration.

missingStatements.text: Jews from anywhere in the world should have the right to immigrate to Israel and become citizens.
missingStatements.rationale: Encouraging aliyah and the ingathering of exiles is a listed foundation of Zionism, distinct from immigration policy in general.

missingStatements.text: A people dispersed in exile should return to and rebuild its ancestral homeland.
missingStatements.rationale: Zionism treats diaspora life as something to end through return to the Land of Israel, in a general form other diaspora nationalisms could also answer.

missingStatements.text: A national language that has fallen out of everyday use should be revived as the language of the state.
missingStatements.rationale: The revival of Hebrew was a central Zionist project, endorsed by the movement in 1913 and kept in the Jerusalem Program's commitment to Hebrew education.

notes: Zionism is a family whose economic and social views follow its sub-strands, so many answers are 0 at low confidence and the profile may fail the salience check. Pew surveys Israeli Jews, a population that includes non-Zionists, and is used only as a proxy for contemporary adherents. Critics describe Zionism as ethnic nationalist or settler colonial, which Wikipedia reports alongside adherents' self-description as a national liberation movement.
